items.title: Allen Toussaint Interview, 1979-03-13
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...King Biscuit Boy. ... And so that's one aspect of the studio.

ctx.x: If you don't object, I'd like to ask you a couple things about how you run the studio. There seems, from what I hear, there's like some sort of different systems. If somebody wants to come in here, pay you for the time, the studio's open to them. You know, so... Bonnie Raitt's recorded here. Paul McCartney's been here. King Biscuit Boy. The Mighty Diamonds. Robert Palmer. And so that's one aspect of the studio. Like, the musician can come here and pay you for the sessions. And you produce... And you produce the…

Unless it can be placed somewhere and they can be reimbursed. For instance, if there's a group and they're not with anyone, they can come in and make a demo session or just record a session. And the studio bill will be calculated, but not issued to them. Then if they want to take it somewhere and try to place it with the company, let someone hear it and see if someone accepts it, they can do that. And if they find someone that accepts it, who will give them fronts, you might call it, which is only to reimburse…
